instruction: Press the juicer's knob down until it reaches its pressed position, then let go.

outcome.real_measurement: Rationale: the env's own press target (qmin + 0.25 (qmax - qmin) = -0.218 rad, model 103105; as v1 / v2): the dial must be at or beyond it at EVERY step of the judged window, i.e. left pressed after the robot has stopped (latching dial: joint stiffness 0, checked by the binding). Real world: joint encoder or an AprilTag on the dial tracked for 1 s after the robot stops.

Rationale: the dial is at rest in the judged window: it moves by at most 0.01 rad (0.6 deg, ~0.25 mm at the 2.4 cm rim) from the window's first step; a dial still being turned moves far more. Real world: same tracking, 1 s.

Rationale: the dial was moved by the robot: >= 1 control step with robot-knob contact impulse accumulated over all physics substeps >= 5e-4 N*s (v1's 0.05 N floor for one 10 ms substep; unchanged from v2). Real world: fingertip tactile / wrist F/T integrated over 50 ms while the fingertip is within 1 cm of the dial.

source.protocol: v3: veritask/adapters/protocol_v3.py (semantics), maniskill_v3.py (recorder, hold, enclosure), maniskill_v3_tasks.py (signals)
source.frozen: 2026-11-14, before any E15 evaluation-set run; thresholds chosen knowing the E10 and E13 reports and the user rulings of 2026-11-14 (not blind to them)
source.rounds: E10 red team (research/results/e10_redteam), E13 red team (research/results/e13_redteam2)

notes: Protocol v3 (veritask/adapters/protocol_v3.py). After the policy's last action the evaluator HOLDS the robot where it stopped (hold A: every arm switched to a pd_joint_pos hold of the joint positions reached at the policy's last step, drive-velocity targets zeroed, grippers keep their last commanded opening; any control mode). It steps until the scene is quiescent for settle.quiet_steps = 10 consecutive control steps (0.5 s: every quiet_max signal under its bound at every step, every quiet_disp group moved <= its bound, largest arm-joint speed <= 0.01 rad/s, measured from joint POSITIONS over each control step: PhysX's reported joint velocity stays at 0.012-0.043 while nothing moves when the robot presses through a held object or closes its fingers on one, E15 development runs; finger joints excluded) and then judges the following 1.0 s window (20 steps); if no quiescence leaves room for the window inside settle.max_seconds = 3.0 s the episode is rejected. End-state terms (trace.window_*) read only the judged window; event terms (trace.count_true / trace.max) read the episode up to the window's end. Hold B (switch, not the default): the evaluator replays the policy's last action and robot joint speed must stay <= settle.robot_speed_max at every window step. Constants: max_seconds 3.0 = room for the slowest legitimate transient seen (a fast-pushed cube at rest 0.3 s after the last action, E13 P23; a held robot settles in < 0.5 s, E15 probe) with margin; quiet_steps 10 = 0.5 s of stillness; robot_speed_max 0.01 rad/s (about 5-8 mm/s at the TCP; a held robot reaches 1e-4 rad/s within 0.5 s, E15 probe; E13's creeping policies ran at 0.04-0.09 rad/s). released = at every step of the judged window: zero robot-object contact impulse (every link of every arm, accumulated over all physics substeps) AND the object is not enclosed by a gripper (enclosure clearance > 2 mm). Proximity without contact and without enclosure is released whatever the link (user ruling 2026-11-14: E10 J7 s2, E13 C23 / C25 / C29 / J25). Rationale: 'then let go' = not holding the object: no contact (release.contact_signals) and not enclosed. Enclosure clearance = sum of the two fingers' PhysX contact-point separations (clipped at 0) for a gripper that has part of the object between its finger pads (inter-finger slab from the finger collision boxes in the hand frame); 1 m when no gripper has the object between its pads. enclosure_margin_m 2 mm: fingers closed on an object read ~0 (grasped cup 0.17 mm, E15 probe; E10 C1 s2 fingers at -0.02 mm), a fully opened Panda gripper around cup 1 reads 7.3-8.2 mm (E13 C23 3.7-4.1 mm per side); 2 mm = 1 mm per side when centred. Real world: gripper opening from the finger encoder vs the object's width at the grasp (camera / CAD), plus zero tactile signal. Knob: latching dial (stiffness 0); a spring-return button needs an event-form contract. The route is not constrained (press, jab, twist, either arm) as long as the dial is left pressed and released. Quiescence for this task: |dial velocity| <= 0.05 rad/s and dial moved <= 0.005 rad over the 10 quiet steps, robot joint speed <= 0.01.
